clue.text: Soldiers fit for another fight

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
an outfit that fits is a match for you

explanation.surface: Troops declared ready to go into battle again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents.

clue.text: In New York, an inn for Japanese

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A Japanese-style hotel opening in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is part of the city name in the surface but signals rearranging YORK into RYOK, with AN added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A ryokan is a traditional Japanese guesthouse.

clue.text: He must control the players or teams become disorderly

indicators.note: become disorderly tells us the letters fall out of their order

explanation.surface: A conductor must keep his musicians in line or the sections fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a conductor of an orchestra, who directs the musicians.

clue.text: Examine a religious group, one operating on a different plane?

definitions.text: one operating on a different plane?

parts.note: to test is to examine
PI is short for pious, religious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Questioning a sect whose members seem to live on a higher spiritual level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word. The plane is an aircraft, not a level of existence: a test pilot flies new or different aeroplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies experimental aircraft, so operates a different plane.

clue.text: Energetic senior editor seen about captive soldier

indicators.note: seen about means the senior word is wrapped around the captive

parts.note: higher means of more senior rank
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A dynamic senior journalist is spotted with a prisoner of war.
explanation.definitionFit: High-powered means dynamic and forceful, full of energy.

clue.text: Nonsense books I produced in a hurry

indicators.note: in places the books and I within the hurry

parts.note: a rush is a hurry
B is short for book, doubled for the plural as pp is for pages

explanation.surface: Silly books knocked out at speed by the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is a link word; 'in' puts BBI inside RUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is worthless talk or writing, just like nonsense.

clue.text: Turning cartwheels can make such a deep impression

definitions.text: Turning cartwheels can make such a deep impression

parts.words: Turning cartwheels can make such a deep impression
parts.note: not gymnastics: the wheels of a cart, rolling over soft ground, carve a groove into it

explanation.surface: A gymnast's cartwheels make a powerful impression on the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a deep track worn into the ground by wheels.

clue.text: Vote with the opposition party

definitions.meaning: to vote against is to ..., said as three words

explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a jolly party, and split up it reads as being one of the no voters.

clue.text: One political representative a number of Germans suggested

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
a Lied is a German song, a musical number

explanation.surface: An MP proposed a certain quota of German people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' looks like a quantity of people but is a song; Lied is the German art song.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied means hinted at or suggested without being said outright.

clue.text: Filly in form leading at Chelten ham, say

definitions.text: Filly in form leading at Chelten ham, say

parts.words: Filly in form leading at Chelten ham, say
parts.note: reads as a racehorse ahead at Cheltenham races, but the filly is a schoolgirl, the form a school class, Cheltenham Ladies' College

explanation.surface: A young mare on good form leads the field at Cheltenham racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham, split across a line on the page, is a racecourse town and home of a famous girls' school; a head girl is the senior pupil leading the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A head girl is the senior schoolgirl chosen to lead the pupils.

clue.text: To express weariness in public could be a mistake

indicators.note: in puts the weary breath within the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
to sigh is to express weariness

explanation.surface: Yawning openly might be a social blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an error made through failing to notice something.

clue.text: Top mark in Greek

parts.note: read as the highest grade given in a Greek exam, but also the first character heading the Greek ...

explanation.surface: The best grade a student can get in Greek class.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter also names a top grade, as in alpha plus.

clue.text: Behave badly in a court, appearing for trial

parts.note: someone who is up before the magistrate is appearing for trial

explanation.surface: A defendant misbehaving in the dock during proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or play up.

clue.text: Moderate caught up in demonstration can become offensive

indicators.note: caught up in places the moderate word within the demonstration word

parts.note: proving is demonstrating, so demonstration here
OK means fair, middling, moderate

explanation.surface: A moderate swept along at a protest rally may turn nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provoking is irritating or annoying, causing offence.

clue.text: Starting instruction, this is how you'll be assessed

definitions.meaning: the call given to runners before a race

definitions.text: this is how you'll be assessed
definitions.meaning: read literally, judged according to the grades you score

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a race starter's call and, taken literally, means judged by your grades.

clue.text: Game editor's request to readers?

definitions.meaning: a children's game in which everyone copies the one at the front
an editor might ask readers to keep up with the leading article, the newspaper leader

explanation.definitionFit: A children's copying game whose name, read literally, asks people to keep up with one's leader column.

clue.text: Found his tables collapsing

indicators.note: collapsing suggests the tables fall into a jumbled heap

explanation.surface: A man discovered his furniture falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find but is the verb meaning to set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up or create it.

clue.text: A top firm introducing first-class line in fashionable resort

indicators.note: introducing means the firm sequence takes the class and line letters inside it

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
CO is short for company, a firm
U means upper-class, top-drawer

explanation.surface: A leading company brings in a first-class route to a chic holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a Mexican beach resort long popular with the jet set.

clue.text: Take action against bacteria, an unusual form of life

parts.note: to counter something is to act against it
a culture is a colony of bacteria grown in a lab

explanation.surface: Fighting germs, which are themselves a strange kind of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterculture is an alternative lifestyle at odds with mainstream society.

clue.text: Sort of vehicle that provides a public service

definitions.meaning: as in a sport ... vehicle or ... van
a company supplying gas, water or electricity

explanation.definitionFit: A utility vehicle is a type of van or truck, and a utility is a supplier of power or water.

clue.text: Write to after arrest, and meet

indicators.note: after puts the written word to behind the arrest phrase

parts.note: to run someone in is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Send a letter once someone is arrested, and then meet them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write' tells us to set down the word 'to' as it is; the count was misread as '4j.'
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to encounter them by chance.

clue.text: Jacket a girl put on king

indicators.note: put on means the girl comes before the king, set upon it in this down clue

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A young woman helped the king into his coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a waterproof hooded jacket.

clue.text: State of a royal child

parts.note: looks like the condition of being a king's son, but means a country ruled by such a royal

explanation.surface: The status of being born to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A princedom is a territory ruled by a prince, or the rank of prince.

clue.text: In which, essentially, you need to take a piece?

definitions.text: In which, essentially, you need to take a piece?

indicators.note: In tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about a situation where you must grab a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'which, essentially', and the whole clue also describes the board game, where capturing pieces is the point.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game players capture each other's pieces.

clue.text: Leader of Government ousted from friendly African state

indicators.note: ousted from means that initial is thrown out of the friendly word

parts.note: benign means kindly, friendly

indicators.note: leader of takes just the initial of the next word

explanation.surface: A head of government is thrown out of a once friendly African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' gives G, and 'ousted from' removes it from BENIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Benin is a West African country, formerly Dahomey.

clue.text: European money, including none that's controlled by French banks

indicators.note: including means the money word holds the nothing within it

parts.note: lire were the currency of Italy before the euro
O, the figure zero, means none

explanation.surface: Euro cash, with nothing left over, held by French banking houses.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks are not financial: a river is held in by its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is a French river, kept in its course by its banks.

clue.text: Alien enemy surrounding dominion, right?

indicators.note: surrounding has the enemy word encircle the dominion word

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a reign is a period of dominion or rule

explanation.surface: Suspicious of an outsider: a hostile alien encircling our territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner is someone from another country, an alien.

clue.text: Young cook

definitions.meaning: newly hatched fish, as a collective noun

explanation.definitionFit: Small young fish are called fry, and to fry is to cook in oil.

clue.text: Wandering account of a post-war decade

definitions.text: Wandering account of a post-war decade

parts.words: Wandering account of a post-war decade
parts.note: Homer's epic tells of ten years of travels after the Trojan War, so a wandering story of a decade following war

explanation.surface: A rambling history of the ten years after the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic narrates Odysseus's ten years of travel home from Troy, and the word now means any long journey.

clue.text: School affected by cut has to secure inferior goods from Us

parts.note: SCH is the shortened form of school
to lock is to secure

explanation.surface: A school hit by budget cuts has to make do with cheap goods from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word; 'affected by cut' says school is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlock is American slang, from Yiddish, for shoddy or cheap merchandise.
